modalLead: Every tag gets a view of its own, with its bookmarks from every page. Tag suggestions know some 51,000 sites and show up in the rows. And a Home Assistant widget switches lights and scenes from the dashboard.

items.text: A view for every tag. Pick a tag in the cloud and see every bookmark with it, from all pages, in one table: related tags, open all, copy links, and rename, merge or remove the tag, with undo.
items.title: A view for every tag

media.alt: The tag view for homelab: every bookmark with the tag from every page, with related tags beside it

items.text: A quieter tag cloud. Three sizes, a count beside each tag, and typing finds one. Shift+click stacks tags and shows how many bookmarks each would add.
Suggestions in the rows. The tag view and the Bookmarks view show suggested tags right after a bookmark's own: click to add, × to turn down, or Add all. Find tags looks up the rows on screen.
items.title: Tag suggestions right in the rows

media.alt: The Bookmarks view with suggested tags after the rows’ own tags, and Add all over the list

items.text: The inbox gets a Tags column, with the same suggested tags and Add all as the Bookmarks view. a adds the suggestion of the link under the cursor.
A catalogue of some 51,000 sites, and Wikidata for the sites it does not know. Only the site's name leaves your server, and you can switch the lookup off in the tags tab.
A tag you take off stays off. The suggestions no longer offer it again for that bookmark.

Home Assistant on your dashboard. Connect with an access token, pick up to 60 entities and lay them out per room. Lights, switches, fans, scenes and scripts switch from the tile; doors, locks and sensors show their state.
items.title: Switch Home Assistant from your dashboard

media.alt: The Home Assistant tile: lights, a scene and sensors, with switches on the tile

items.text: A key legend under the grid. Three lines with the keys that matter; Shift+Z switches it off and on.
Shift+F filters the page in the search bar's style, with the match marked in the names that are left.
Shorter tours that cover the main features. Shift+K plays the dashboard tour again; each view has a Tour button.
Choose the animation speed, or switch off the animations in views and modals.
Two devices no longer undo each other's work: new pages, renamed pages, categories and finders made on one device survive a save on another.
Switching pages no longer keeps the folded categories and widgets of the page you left.
Monitoring checks every service in turn on a busy host, and maintenance windows keep their hours when the clocks change.
A calendar widget no longer fails for a minute after a reload.
The inbox shows a link saved from the extension or another tab as soon as you open it, without a reload.
